clue.text: Member's lobby consumed by matter

indicators.note: something consumed is swallowed up, so one piece ends up inside the other

parts.note: matter in the medical sense: discharge from a wound
a hall is an entrance lobby

explanation.surface: A lobby belonging to a member of some club or parliament, swallowed up by business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member's' reads as a possessive, but it is 'Member is': the definition plus a link. P(HALL)US.
explanation.definitionFit: Member is a polite or euphemistic word for the male organ, which is what the answer names.

clue.text: Did Harry start to die following epidemic?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the single letter is sent to the end

parts.note: a plague is a widespread outbreak

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A question whether Prince Harry, or some Harry, began dying after an outbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb to harass.
explanation.definitionFit: To harry someone is to pester them persistently, and plagued means tormented or harassed in the same way.

clue.text: Going on at entertaining buffoon endlessly

indicators.note: a host entertaining guests has them inside, so one word holds the other
endlessly means without its last letter

explanation.surface: Something happening at a show hosted by a clown who never stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A(FOO)T.
explanation.definitionFit: Afoot means in progress or under way, as when plans are afoot, so it means happening.

clue.text: Church singers caught waterfowl?

indicators.note: to catch what someone says is to hear it, so the sound counts

parts.note: whimsical birds of a lake; in British speech clerk is said 'clark'

explanation.surface: Church choristers catching ducks, or being caught.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags invented birds, larks of the lake. Lay clerks are paid adult singers in a cathedral choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Lay clerks are the professional adult men who sing in English cathedral choirs alongside the boy choristers.

clue.text: Row about university left dons worthless deal in the end

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the group is wrapped by the outer letters
in the end points to the final letter of each word

parts.note: c is short for circa, about
U is the abbreviation for university
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An argument about a university after the dons leave a useless agreement at the last minute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' look like university teachers, but it is the verb to put on: S(CUL)L.
explanation.definitionFit: To scull is to row a boat using a pair of oars or a single oar at the stern.

clue.text: Distil rare gin closer to boiling point?

indicators.note: distilling breaks a liquid down and reforms it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Instructions for distilling unusual gin, heating it nearer to the boil.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone more furious is figuratively nearer to boiling over, hence the question mark on this playful definition.

clue.text: Appealed to law to stop free trade agreement's completion

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so the law sits inside the other letters
set free, the letters are loosed into a new order
the completion of a word is its final letter

parts.note: an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: Legislation brought in to halt the completion of a free trade deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free trade agreement' reads as one phrase but splits into anagram signal, fodder, and a source of one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that attracted you appealed to you, drawing your interest, so the past tenses match.

clue.text: Sense of shame reduced deceit over time

indicators.note: reduced means made shorter, so the last letter goes

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Remorse that has dwindled over the years for a past deception.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' puts the shortened deceit above the time.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilt is the feeling of remorse or culpability after wrongdoing, a sense of shame.

clue.text: Involve troublemaker and Queen perhaps in story

indicators.note: in places one word within the other

parts.note: a queen is a female cat

explanation.surface: A tale involving a mischief-maker and perhaps the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen' suggests royalty, but breeders call a female cat a queen; the 'perhaps' flags the example. IMP + LI(CAT)E.
explanation.definitionFit: To implicate someone is to show them to be involved or connected, especially in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Discharge on electronic screen boosted

indicators.note: boosted means pushed upwards, which in a down clue reads the letters bottom to top

explanation.surface: A display on an electronic screen, enlarged and turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + E VEIL read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To relieve someone of a duty is to discharge them, freeing them from it.

clue.text: Adult wasted pounds working with unknown adviser

indicators.note: to pound is to shut animals in an enclosure, so one word holds the others

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A grown-up spends money recklessly on an unidentified consultant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money, but it is the verb: the thin word impounds the working unknown, giving A + G(ON Y)AUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: An agony aunt writes a newspaper advice column, answering readers' personal problems, so she is an adviser.

clue.text: Drive forward author's brief career

indicators.note: a brief version is cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the author speaking of himself says 'I am'
to career is to rush along, as is to pelt

explanation.surface: A writer's short-lived career, pushed on by circumstance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' is a verb here, meaning to race.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to push or urge something onward, a direct synonym for propelling it ahead.

clue.text: What, ultimately, college student gets up to

indicators.note: to get something is to take it in, so one piece is received inside the others
ultimately points at the very end of the preceding word

parts.note: the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: A question about what a university student is getting up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets up to' reads as one phrase, but the split is 'gets' and 'up to': UN(T)IL, with the T dropped between the N and the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Until and up to both mean as far as a given time, as in working until or up to midnight.

clue.text: In any case, American is no smarter than anyone else

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a chiefly US adverb for at any rate
second meaning, split as two words: having the smallest amount of wisdom

explanation.surface: A dig that Americans are, whatever else, no cleverer than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, LEAST WISE, the answer describes whoever is lowest in wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: Leastwise is a mainly American adverb for at least or anyway, and as a phrase it describes minimal wisdom.

clue.text: Question validity of trend looking back on record run

parts.note: R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: a tide of opinion is a trend

explanation.surface: Doubting whether a fashion that harks back to a record-breaking run means anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is a link here: in an across clue the reversed trend simply follows the record and the run. R is the cricket scorer's run.
explanation.definitionFit: To discredit a claim is to cast doubt on it, so challenging its trustworthiness and truth.

clue.text: Corrupt agent means to ignore new player's identity

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so the letters are scrambled
to ignore something leaves it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A dishonest agent plans to snub a fresh actor's persona.
explanation.walkthrough: One N is dropped from the fodder before it is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage name is the professional name an actor performs under, their identity as a player.

clue.text: What helps to regulate beating of figures surrounding boxer?

indicators.note: surrounding means going round, so one word wraps the other

explanation.surface: Numbers surrounding a fighter, and a puzzle over who controls the beating he gives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beating' suggests a fight, but it is the heart's beat. DIGIT(ALI)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Digitalis, from foxglove, is a drug used to slow and steady the heartbeat in heart failure.

clue.text: Stone and lead taken from ancient passage

indicators.note: the lead is the front position, so the opening letter is taken

parts.note: a gate is a way through

explanation.surface: A stone and some lead removed from an old corridor, as an archaeologist might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' sounds like the metal, but it means the leading letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agate is a banded semi-precious variety of chalcedony, a kind of gemstone.

clue.text: Doctor lamenting association with certain political views?

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: A physician grieving over joining a political camp.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's alignment is its siding with a particular ideology or bloc, as in political alignment.

clue.text: Stupid man wiped out in financial failures

indicators.note: wiped out means erased, so those letters are removed from the longer word

parts.note: a man is referred to as he

explanation.surface: A foolish fellow who lost everything in a series of economic collapses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stupid man' reads as one phrase, but 'Stupid' alone is the definition. CRA(HE)SHES with HE removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass describes gross insensitivity or lack of intelligence, a near synonym for being dense or foolish.

clue.text: Greens almost get behind Conservative group

indicators.note: almost means short of the whole, so the last letter is dropped
behind means coming after, so the shortened verb goes last

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Green Party members nearly back a Tory faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greens' sounds political beside 'Conservative', but it means vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabbage is a leafy vegetable, and green vegetables are collectively called greens.

clue.text: Spiritual quality of columns in gallery

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a British theatre
columns as rows or ranks of people

explanation.surface: Something holy about pillars standing in an art gallery or church.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the cheap upper gallery of a theatre, so the gallery wraps the columns.
explanation.definitionFit: Godliness is devoutness or piety, a spiritual virtue of someone who lives reverently.

clue.text: First pair leaving yesterday somehow went wrong

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the order is left open
the opening two letters depart from the word

explanation.surface: The leading couple dropped out yesterday, and something went awry.
explanation.definitionFit: To stray is to wander off the right path, so it means erring or going astray morally.

clue.text: Guard porter possibly charged with base act

indicators.note: charged means loaded or filled, so the drink holds the other pieces

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: A security guard or hotel porter accused of a contemptible deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Porter' and 'charged' read as a doorman facing a criminal charge. BE(E FEAT)ER; beefeaters are the Yeomen Warders at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Beefeater is a ceremonial guard at the Tower of London, so the word is a type of guard.

clue.text: Ogle sexy men regularly seen out of bed

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
someone out of bed is up

explanation.surface: Leering at attractive men who have been spotted out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye up someone is to look them over with sexual interest, which is exactly what ogling means.

clue.text: Bits of litter spread over street

parts.note: dye or ink that spreads runs

indicators.note: over means turned upside down, which in a down clue reads the letters upwards

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: Pieces of rubbish scattered across a road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Litter' looks like rubbish but means a brood of young animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Runts are the smallest, weakest animals in a litter of piglets or puppies.

clue.text: Free article about lowest of the low?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined pair is read backwards

explanation.surface: A free item in a magazine about the most wretched people of all.
explanation.walkthrough: RID + AN read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the very bottom point, so it is the lowest of the low points, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Prevent Right taking away vote

indicators.note: taking away means removing, so a letter is subtracted

parts.note: dexter is the heraldic term for right
a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: The political right trying to stop people voting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks political, but it is the heraldic word for the right side of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: To deter someone is to discourage or stop them from acting, so it means to prevent.

clue.text: Saw Bill get older

parts.note: a bill is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: Someone spotted Bill getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past of see, but it is the noun for an old proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is a traditional proverb or saying, just as an adage is a well-worn maxim.

clue.text: Leyton, not having Circle Line, developed in moderate fashion

indicators.note: developed means reshaped into a new form, so the letters are rearranged
not having means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written; Leyton is a district of east London
a circle is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: Leyton, in east London, lacking the Circle Line Tube service, grew up modestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle Line' is a London Underground line, but here it splits: Circle is the O removed, Line is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting leniently means showing mercy and tolerance rather than severity, a mild or moderate manner.

clue.text: Excuses of English politician in kinky sext case

indicators.note: a case surrounds its contents, so the shuffled word goes around the others
kinky means twisted, so the letters are bent into a new order

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English MP's explanations in a scandal over a racy text message.
explanation.walkthrough: A sext is a sexually explicit text message; 'case' looks like a scandal but means the outer wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to excuse them from a duty or obligation, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Took action about performer almost getting stitched up

indicators.note: about means around, so the legal action goes round the other piece
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a turn is a variety act or performer

explanation.surface: Someone sued over an entertainer who was nearly framed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitched up' suggests being framed; here it is literal, as with a wound. SU(TUR)ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Sutured means sewn together with surgical stitches, the literal sense of stitching a wound closed.
